21915-directions-for-navigating-on-part-:
Sailors on a dangerous coast get exact orders in James Cook's Directions for Navigating on Part of the South Coast of Newfoundland. Cook surveyed the coast by order of Commodore Palliser, governor of Newfoundland, before his fame as a Pacific explorer. The book, with its chart, includes the islands of St. Pierre and Miquelon. Cape Chapeaurouge in Placentia Bay is fixed at latitude 46 degrees 53 minutes north, and so it goes, headland by headland.

Bays, harbors, rocks, landmarks, depths of water, currents, and tides are all set down from the actual survey. The spelling is old, and the lost frontispiece chart is missed, but the working value remains. It is Cook the surveyor at his first trade: patient, exact, and lifesaving on paper.
